title: Precision traffic simulator and golden probe for quant accuracy validation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Build an automated validation harness that simulates customer traffic distributions, injects curated golden prompts, and exercises FP8/INT8 calibration artifacts to produce deterministic pass/fail decisions before quantized rollouts. This harness — the Precision Traffic Simulator + Golden Probe (PTSGP) — will be used by the quant CI pipeline and by release engineers during canary and dedicated deployments.

Scope:
- Traffic simulator that replays anonymized production traces (token length, role distribution, streaming vs batch) and synthesizes adversarial variants to stress calibration edges.
- Golden prompt collection pipeline with metadata tags (cohort, lingua, prompt-type, expected-metric-signatures) and automated freshness scoring.
- Multi-arm gating: precision gate (response fidelity vs FP32 baseline), stability gate (determinism under KV-cache/continuous-batching), and distribution gate (embedding similarity / distributional KL).
- Metric suite including: token-level log-prob drift, top-k token accuracy, BLEU/ROUGE for generation tasks, embedding cosine similarity, perplexity delta, and hallucination indicators (entity recall against golden ground-truth).
- Per-cohort dynamic thresholds and weighted scoring to surface regressions that matter for critical customers.
- CI integration: must run as pre-merge smoke for quant PRs and as part of nightly regression; produce machine-readable verdict (pass/fail) with provenance.

Non-goals: full A/B user-facing rollout; model retraining or altering quant strategy automatically (this remains a human-reviewed step).
acceptance_criteria: PTSGP can replay a representative 10k-request synthetic workload derived from production traces with configurable token-length distributions and role mixes.
Golden prompt pipeline supports tagging and automated freshness scoring; at least 500 unique golden prompts spanning 10 cohorts ingested.
Three gates implemented: precision, stability, distribution — harness fails a run if any gate misses its cohort threshold.
Metrics computed per-request and aggregated per-cohort: log-prob delta, top-k accuracy, embedding cosine, perplexity delta, and a hallucination score. All metrics stored in CI artifact JSON.
Harness integrates with quant calibration artifacts (FP8 and INT8 profiles) and can run with both quant and FP32 baselines for direct comparisons.
End-to-end run time for a standard smoke suite (500 prompts) < 20 minutes on CI worker with 1 GPU; verdict exported to release dashboard and GitHub PR check.
Automated rollback trigger: when nightly runs exceed defined weighted-failure-rate for critical cohorts, an alert is created and rollout is blocked (manual override recorded).
implementation_notes:
Architecture: lightweight runner that can execute on CI and on dedicated staging clusters. Two primary components: 1) Traffic simulator service (Go) that samples request shapes and sequences; 2) Probe runner (Python) that formats prompts, runs model calls through the runtime, collects telemetry and computes metrics. Use existing telemetry SDK for token-level logs and tracing.

Data and privacy: replay uses fully anonymized traces; golden prompts are scrubbed of PII and stored in a secured dataset. Access controlled via existing RBAC.

Performance considerations: batch and KV-cache behavior will be simulated; ensure harness can toggle continuous batching parameters to reproduce production modes. Keep GPU memory and token budget knobs configurable.

Extensibility: gates should be pluggable — teams can add new metrics (e.g., factuality checks) without modifying core harness. Store metric definitions in plain YAML in the repo (not embedded in code).
test_plan: Spike 1 (week 1): Build minimal traffic simulator that replays static 1k-request trace and validates end-to-end runner with FP32 baseline.
Spike 2 (week 2): Implement golden prompt ingestion and tagging; run 200 golden prompts across FP32 and a single INT8 profile and compare metrics.
Integration (week 3): Add multi-arm gates and threshold config; wire CI job and GitHub status; produce sample PR check artifact.
Nightly (week 4): Run full 10k synthetic workload on staging; validate storage of artifacts in s3 and dashboard integration; tune thresholds using historical baselines.
Canary run (post-merge): Shadow traffic run with quant profile on a small percentage of dedicated capacity; verify harness verdicts align with on-call observations.
